title: Pin `git_repo` fixture initial branch to `main` in `tests/adapters/test_subprocess_git.py`
summary: The `git_repo` async fixture in `tests/adapters/test_subprocess_git.py:11-19` runs bare `git init` and leaves the initial branch name up to the host's git config. On the GitHub Actions ubuntu-24.04 runner there is no global `init.defaultBranch`, so git falls back to its compiled-in default (currently `master`), and the two new tests that pass the literal ref `"main"` to `SubprocessGitService.is_ancestor` / `SubprocessGitService.diff_summary` fail because `main` is not a valid local ref. Fix: add `-b main` to the existing `git init` call in the fixture, matching the short-form convention already in use elsewhere in this repo. The change is a single token added to an existing argv list — no new helper, fixture, parameter, or abstraction. No production code under `src/kodezart/` changes; no assertion is weakened; no test is skipped or renamed; the unknown-ref `RuntimeError` contract pinned by `test_is_ancestor_raises_on_unknown_ref` is preserved.
context:
## Why this change is being made

The open consolidation PR on branch `kodezart/fix-ralph-post-merge-consolidation-b4caf4dd-ralph-7c0974a9` has CI failing at the pytest step of `make check`. Ruff and mypy are already clean. Two newly-added tests in `tests/adapters/test_subprocess_git.py` fail on the GitHub Actions Ubuntu runner while passing locally:

- `test_is_ancestor_returns_false_when_not_ancestor` (line 202)
- `test_diff_summary_returns_changeset_digest` (line 301)

## Root cause — clue by clue

1. The async `git_repo` fixture (`tests/adapters/test_subprocess_git.py:11-19`) creates a tmp repo via `await _run_git(["git", "init"], cwd=repo)` at line 15 with NO initial-branch flag. The fixture commits a `README.md` to lock in HEAD but never pins the initial branch name.
2. Per the `git-init` documentation, without `-b/--initial-branch` git falls back to `init.defaultBranch`; if that is unset, git falls back to its compiled-in default, which is currently `master` (the docs note this only changes to `main` in Git 3.0). Source: https://git-scm.com/docs/git-init.
3. The developer's machine has `init.defaultBranch=main` in user-level git config, so the fixture's initial branch is `main` locally — the two tests' hardcoded `"main"` ref resolves and they pass.
4. The `actions/runner-images` ubuntu-24.04 image ships git 2.54.0 with NO global `init.defaultBranch` set — the runner's initial branch is therefore `master`. The literal `"main"` does not name any local ref on CI. Source: https://github.com/actions/runner-images/blob/main/images/ubuntu/Ubuntu2404-Readme.md.
5. `git merge-base --is-ancestor main HEAD` exits 128 with `fatal: Not a valid object name: 'main'`, and `git diff --name-only main..feat-x` exits 128 with `fatal: ambiguous argument 'main..feat-x'`. The production adapter at `src/kodezart/adapters/subprocess_git_service.py` (`is_ancestor` via `_run_with_exit_codes` allowing only `{0,1}`; `diff_summary` via `_run_output` which raises on any non-zero exit) correctly re-raises these as `RuntimeError`. pytest records the unhandled `RuntimeError` as test failure.
6. The contract that unknown refs surface as `RuntimeError` is pinned by `test_is_ancestor_raises_on_unknown_ref` (`tests/adapters/test_subprocess_git.py:227`). Watson's instinct — "make the adapter tolerate unknown refs" — would silently break that contract and is explicitly forbidden by the deliverable. The adapter is correct; the **test fixture is the only thing host-coupled**.

## Why other tests in the same file don't fail on CI

The other `"main"` references in the file fall into two protocol categories that do not consult the local refs database:

- **Push refspecs `HEAD:refs/heads/main`** (lines 242, 293). In a refspec `<src>:<dst>`, the source side is the local ref to push (here `HEAD`, a built-in symbolic ref that always exists) and the destination side is the ref to *create* on the remote. The destination `refs/heads/main` is materialized on the remote by the push itself — no local `main` ref is required for the operation to succeed.
- **`git ls-remote --heads origin …`** (lines 245, 257, 297, via `remote_branch_sha`). `ls-remote` speaks the git wire protocol to the remote and enumerates *the remote's* refs; it never reads the local repository's refs database. Whether the local initial branch is `master` or `main` is irrelevant.

Both categories continue to pass on CI; leave them as is.

## Why this exact mechanism, not alternatives

- `git init -b main` (equivalent to the long form `--initial-branch=main`) has been supported since **git 2.28** per https://git-scm.com/docs/git-init, and the ubuntu-24.04 runner ships **git 2.54.0** per the runner-images Readme — the flag is universally available.
- The short form `-b` is the **established convention in this repo** (see precedents below). Matching it minimizes review surface and lint diff.
- A per-repo `git config init.defaultBranch main` issued AFTER `git init` is a no-op for the already-initialized repo (anti-pattern explicitly forbidden in the deliverable).
- Mutating `--global` git config from the test suite would leak across the host and is explicitly forbidden.
- A `git branch -m master main` rename works but is more code, drops fixture locality, and silently no-ops on hosts where the initial branch is already `main`.

## Runtime/complexity cost — KISS / YAGNI posture

The fix is **a single token added to an existing argv list** (two if you count `-b` and `main` separately): no new helper function, no new fixture, no new parameter, no new conftest entry, no new conditional, no new abstraction. The implementing engineer should resist any expansion (e.g., a "make_test_repo" utility, a parametrised branch-name fixture, or asession-scoped `init.defaultBranch` env var) — none of those is justified by the failure mode being fixed.

## Cross-codebase consistency check (precedents confirm the short form)

A repository-wide search confirms `tests/adapters/test_subprocess_git.py:15` is the ONLY non-`--bare` `git init` call in the suite whose initial branch name is left to the runner's `init.defaultBranch`. Every other test that needs `main` to exist as a local ref already pins it with the **short form `-b main`**:

- `tests/adapters/test_git_branch_merger.py:50` → `await _git(["git", "init", "-b", "main"], cwd=repo)`
- `tests/adapters/test_git_worktree_provider.py:195` → `await _run_git(["git", "init", "-b", "main"], cwd=upstream)`
- `tests/integration/test_workflow_e2e.py:60` → `await _git(["git", "init", "-b", "main"], cwd=repo)`

`tests/conftest.py:15-25` defines an autouse session-scoped `_git_test_identity` fixture that only sets `GIT_AUTHOR_*` / `GIT_COMMITTER_*` env vars — unrelated to branch defaults and must be preserved.

## Documentation consulted

- `git-init` man page — flag semantics and version introduction (Git 2.28); long and short forms are equivalent: https://git-scm.com/docs/git-init
- `actions/runner-images` ubuntu-24.04 image — confirms `git 2.54.0` preinstalled, no global `init.defaultBranch`: https://github.com/actions/runner-images/blob/main/images/ubuntu/Ubuntu2404-Readme.md
- pytest-asyncio async-fixture concept (confirms current fixture shape is idiomatic; only the subprocess argv changes): https://pytest-asyncio.readthedocs.io/en/latest/concepts.html

## Lint / type framework compliance

- Ruff (`pyproject.toml:51-71`): `target-version = "py312"`, `line-length = 88`, select `E,W,F,I,B,C4,UP,N,ANN,S,A,ARG,RUF`, with `tests/**/*.py` per-file ignores `S101, ARG001, ARG002, ANN, S108`. Adding `"-b"` and `"main"` as string elements to an existing list triggers no new lint findings; the added inline comment is well under the 88-column limit.
- Mypy (`pyproject.toml:35-49`): `strict`, `disallow_any_explicit`, `plugins = ["pydantic.mypy"]`. Production code is untouched. The fixture's signature, types, and `_run_git` call shape are unchanged — no type-checker impact.
- Anti-patterns honored: no skip marker, no assertion weakening, no `try/except RuntimeError` wrapping, no production-side tolerance of unknown refs, no global git-config mutation, no post-`git init` `git config init.defaultBranch`, no rename, no compensating new test.

references.note: The async `git_repo` fixture. Line 15 is the offending `await _run_git(["git", "init"], cwd=repo)` call that omits the initial-branch flag and inherits the runner's `init.defaultBranch` (which on ubuntu-24.04 is unset → falls back to `master`). The fix lives entirely on this line.

`test_is_ancestor_returns_false_when_not_ancestor` — line 224 passes the literal `"main"` to `git_service.is_ancestor`. Fails on CI because `main` is not a local ref when the fixture's initial branch is `master`. Must pass after the fix without assertion change.
`test_diff_summary_returns_changeset_digest` — line 312 passes `"main"` as `base_ref` to `git_service.diff_summary`. Same root cause; same expectation post-fix.
`test_is_ancestor_raises_on_unknown_ref` — the contract test that pins the adapter's `RuntimeError` behavior on truly unknown refs. MUST continue to pass; the fix must not weaken this contract.

`SubprocessGitService.is_ancestor` and `SubprocessGitService.diff_summary` (plus their helpers `_run_with_exit_codes` and `_run_output`). Correctly raise `RuntimeError` on the `fatal: Not a valid object name` / `fatal: ambiguous argument` exit-128 path. NO change required — referenced here as the load-bearing link between the failure path observed in CI and the contract that must be preserved.
`_git_test_identity` autouse session fixture — sets `GIT_AUTHOR_*` / `GIT_COMMITTER_*` env vars only. Unrelated to branch defaults; must be preserved (do not weaken or remove).
Precedent for the short-form pin: `await _git(["git", "init", "-b", "main"], cwd=repo)`. Match this convention.
Third short-form precedent: `await _git(["git", "init", "-b", "main"], cwd=repo)`. Confirmed path — the file lives under `tests/integration/`, not `tests/workflow/`.
CI runs on `ubuntu-latest` (currently ubuntu-24.04), which has no global `init.defaultBranch` — the host-config divergence that exposes the bug.
`check: lint type-check test` — the make target that fails on CI. After the fix, all three sub-targets must exit 0.
Mypy strict / disallow_any_explicit and Ruff selections with the `tests/**/*.py` per-file ignores already cover the added literals and the inline comment; no rule disabled, no new lint.

requiredChanges.description: In the `git_repo` async fixture (lines 11-19), change line 15 from `await _run_git(["git", "init"], cwd=repo)` to `await _run_git(["git", "init", "-b", "main"], cwd=repo)`. Use the short form `-b main` to match the established repo convention (precedents at `tests/adapters/test_git_branch_merger.py:50`, `tests/adapters/test_git_worktree_provider.py:195`, `tests/integration/test_workflow_e2e.py:60`). Immediately above that line, add a one-line inline comment so future readers don't wonder why the flag is there: `# pin initial branch so 'main' is a valid local ref independent of host gitconfig`. No other line in the file is modified. Specifically: do NOT rename the fixture or the two failing tests; do NOT touch the assertions in `test_is_ancestor_returns_false_when_not_ancestor` (line 224 `is False`) or `test_diff_summary_returns_changeset_digest` (lines 313-315 membership checks); do NOT add `pytest.mark.skip`/`skipif`; do NOT wrap calls in `try`/`except RuntimeError`; do NOT issue a separate `git config init.defaultBranch` after `git init` (no-op anti-pattern); do NOT touch the bare-repo `git init --bare` calls at lines 88, 95, 141, 239, 255, 290 or the non-bare `git init` at line 267 (used by `test_remote_branch_sha_raises_on_unexpected_exit`, which intentionally does not depend on local `main`).
requiredChanges.rationale: Pins the fixture's initial branch to `main` for every test that uses it so the literal ref `"main"` resolves to a valid local ref on any runner regardless of the host's `init.defaultBranch`. The `-b` flag is supported since git 2.28 (https://git-scm.com/docs/git-init); the ubuntu-24.04 runner ships git 2.54.0 (https://github.com/actions/runner-images/blob/main/images/ubuntu/Ubuntu2404-Readme.md), so the flag is universally available. Short form `-b` matches the three precedents in this repo, so the diff is conventional. The fix is fully on the test side; production code in `src/kodezart/adapters/subprocess_git_service.py` is correct and continues to raise `RuntimeError` on truly unknown refs, preserving the contract pinned by `test_is_ancestor_raises_on_unknown_ref` at line 227.

outOfScope: Any change to production code in `src/kodezart/` — the adapter is correct and the `RuntimeError`-on-unknown-ref contract must not regress.
Renaming, skipping, or re-asserting the two currently-failing tests.
Adding new tests to 'compensate' for the failure — the two existing tests must pass on their own once the fixture is fixed.
Modifying `tests/conftest.py` `_git_test_identity` autouse fixture (unrelated to branch defaults; preserve as is).

Modifying the `git_repo` fixtures in `tests/adapters/test_git_change_persister.py:26-37` or `tests/adapters/test_git_worktree_provider.py:26-35` (both fixtures are literally named `git_repo` — verified) or any other tmp-repo-initializing fixture in those files. They are not failing on CI and are outside the scope of this ticket.
Mutating the developer's or runner's user-level / global git config from inside the test suite (no `git config --global …`).
Issuing `git config init.defaultBranch main` AFTER `git init` — no-op for the already-initialized repo.
Introducing any new helper, parametrised fixture, conftest entry, or repo-creation utility — the failure mode is fixed by adding `-b main` to one existing argv list.
Bumping the runner image, pinning git version, or changing `.github/workflows/check.yml`.
